Please return the output in a JSON format that complies with the following schema as specified in JSON Schema:
{"properties": {"statements": {"description": "The generated statements", "items": {"type": "string"}, "title": "Statements", "type": "array"}}, "required": ["statements"], "title": "StatementGeneratorOutput", "type": "object"}Do not use single quotes in your response but double quotes,properly escaped with a backslash.

--------EXAMPLES-----------
Example 1
Input: {
    "question": "Who was Albert Einstein and what is he best known for?",
    "answer": "He was a German-born theoretical physicist, widely acknowledged to be one of the greatest and most influential physicists of all time. He was best known for developing the theory of relativity, he also made important contributions to the development of the theory of quantum mechanics."

The CCC uniform not only makes you look good, but it also protects you. It is included as part of your membership in the CCC. The uniform includes a soft cap, shirt, pants, hard hat, steel-toe boots, and gloves.\nuser: thank you. What does CCC’s Core Training program is for? What course are offered during the training?",
    "answer": "According to page 1, CCC’s Core Training program gives Corpsmembers the knowledge and skills needed to succeed in the CCC and beyond. It includes:\n\n- COMET (Corpsmember Orientation, Motivation, Education, and Training): Required for all applicants to become official CCC members.\n- Conservation Awareness Program (CAP): Builds appreciation for California’s natural resources and understanding of members’ roles as conservationists, consumers, and citizens—the “why” behind their work.\n- Career Development and Transition (CDT): Prepares members for employment, college, and/or technical education through self-assessment, exploring options, résumé development, and interview skills.\n\nMembers who complete Core Training and a full year in the CCC may be eligible for the CCC Brad Duncan Scholarship."
}

statements: According to page 1, the California Conservation Corps Core Training program provides Corpsmembers with the knowledge and skills needed to succeed in the California Conservation Corps and beyond.
The California Conservation Corps Core Training program includes COMET, meaning Corpsmember Orientation, Motivation, Education, and Training.
COMET is required for all applicants to become official California Conservation Corps members.
The California Conservation Corps Core Training program includes the Conservation Awareness Program (CAP).
The Conservation Awareness Program builds appreciation for California’s natural resources.
The Conservation Awareness Program develops understanding of California Conservation Corps members’ roles as conservationists, consumers, and citizens.
The Conservation Awareness Program explains the purpose behind California Conservation Corps members’ work.
The California Conservation Corps Core Training program includes Career Development and Transition (CDT).
Career Development and Transition prepares California Conservation Corps members for employment, college, and/or technical education.
Career Development and Transition includes self-assessment, exploration of options, résumé development, and interview skills.
California Conservation Corps members completing Core Training and a full year in the California Conservation Corps may be eligible for the CCC Brad Duncan Scholarship.
